# FreeWilly

> A free Windows (10/11) desktop app for installing and driving Docker without Docker
> Desktop. It installs upstream Moby (pinned by version and SHA-256) into a WSL2
> distribution it owns, serves the Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` that the
> `docker` CLI, Compose and every other client already look for, and shows containers in
> one window. Per-user install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FreeWilly` with no administrator
> prompt, no Windows service, no telemetry and no account. Built in C# (.NET 10 — WinForms
> tray, WPF window on the built-in Fluent theme, and an Engine API client with no NuGet
> dependency).

**Nothing has been published to download yet** — building from source with the .NET 10 SDK
is currently the only way to run it. The engine (preflight, provisioning, start/stop, the
pipe, the API client, the event stream, the tray icon), the container window, the per-user
installer and the workflow that drafts a release from a tag all exist; what has not happened
is the tag. The line-by-line picture, with the reason each exists, is in
[`docs/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/alegauss/freewilly/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md) and
[`docs/CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/alegauss/freewilly/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md).

This is an unofficial, open-source community project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed
by, or sponsored by Docker, Inc. "Docker" and "Docker Desktop" are trademarks of Docker,
Inc.; this tool installs the Apache-2.0 licensed Moby engine and Docker CLI as published
upstream, unmodified. Apache-2.0 is the project's stated licence, in `LICENSE`, with a
`NOTICE` covering the bundled upstream binaries.

## For agents

This site answers a coding agent in files it can grep, not only in hydrated markup. Every
route has a Markdown twin beside it — the same page, converted from the same render, with
the navigation, the footer and the call to action dropped. Read `<route>/index.md` instead
of the HTML: the landing page is
[`/index.md`](https://alegauss.github.io/freewilly/index.md). The full list of routes,
their twins and their byte sizes is in
[`manifest.json`](https://alegauss.github.io/freewilly/manifest.json).

## Why it exists

The engine is free and always was — Moby and the `docker` CLI are Apache-2.0. What costs
money, and what a managed corporate laptop often cannot install, is the desktop wrapper
around them. FreeWilly is a different wrapper: same upstream engine, no licence to count
seats against, nothing resident, and an uninstall that cannot take anything of yours with
it.

## Features

- **Preflight (`freewilly --preflight`)**: four rows, each with the action that fixes it —
  Windows build (19041 or later), hardware virtualization, WSL2, and any rival container
  engine that owns the `docker` command or the `docker_engine` pipe. It changes nothing,
  prints a person-readable report or `--json` for an installer, and exits 1 while a
  blocking row is not green, so nothing is copied to disk on a machine that cannot host an
  engine. The virtualization row reads the hypervisor bit *before* the firmware bit,
  because Windows reports the firmware bit as false once a hypervisor has claimed it — the
  naive order tells a plainly virtualizing machine to go and enable virtualization in its
  BIOS.
- **Unattended provisioning (`freewilly --provision`)**: seven named steps, stopping
  at the first failure rather than reporting six consequences of one cause. Downloads and
  verifies Alpine's minirootfs, Docker's static Linux engine binaries and Docker's Windows
  CLI zip against digests recorded in this repository (not served by the same host as the
  file); reads the engine tarball's member list locally to check the required binaries are
  present before WSL is touched; imports a WSL2 distribution named `freewilly` that this
  tool owns rather than the user's own distro; installs the binaries inside it with one
  non-interactive `sh` script under `set -e` (apk adds `iptables` and `socat`, `wsl.conf`
  sets `systemd=false`); and places `docker.exe` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FreeWilly\bin` for an
  installer to put on PATH. `--plan` prints every pinned version, digest and path and
  reaches nothing; `--acquire` downloads and verifies and stops before WSL2 is involved.
- **Start, stop, and a state that is never ahead of the truth (`--run`, `--stop`,
  `--status`)**: starts the distribution and the daemon and reports Running only once the
  engine actually answers. The three ways it goes wrong — the distribution is not
  provisioned, the daemon starts and dies, or the daemon runs and nothing on Windows serves
  the pipe — are named separately because they have three different remedies.
- **The `docker_engine` named pipe**: a Linux `dockerd` cannot create a Windows named pipe,
  so FreeWilly serves it and forwards each connection over `wsl.exe`'s stdio to `socat`
  inside the distribution and on to `/var/run/docker.sock`. The pipe's ACL grants the
  current user account and nobody else — which is the reason it is a pipe and not a
  forwarded TCP port, since the Engine API is equivalent to root on the machine and any
  local process can reach a port. Because the pipe name is the standard one, the CLI,
  Compose, Testcontainers and IDE plugins find the engine with no `DOCKER_HOST` and no
  configuration. **On the Windows side.** A Linux client inside the user's own WSL2
  distribution cannot dial a Windows pipe and reaches nothing; the Windows `docker.exe`
  invoked from a Linux shell does work, through WSL interop, but it is a Windows process
  and reads every path it is handed as a Windows path. There is no per-distribution
  integration and it is a stated non-goal: writing a CLI and a socket into a user's own
  distribution is what this project refuses, and it would hand the Engine API to every
  distribution when the pipe's ACL exists to hold it to one account.
- **Engine API client with zero dependencies**: HTTP and JSON over the named pipe, pinned to
  Engine API `v1.43` (an unversioned path is answered with the daemon's newest version, so a
  daemon upgrade could change a response shape under a client that asked for nothing). It is
  a `NamedPipeClientStream` handed to .NET's own `SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback` — no
  NuGet package, and no spawning `docker.exe` once per refresh.
- **The event stream**: reads `/events` as the daemon writes it and re-opens the stream after
  every break, so a container started in any terminal appears without a refresh, and nothing
  in this project polls. Only the events that change a container list cost a read.
- **Tray icon**: the engine state as a *shape*, with colour only reinforcing it — a filled
  disc for running, a ring with a gap for starting, a plain ring for stopped. At 16 pixels a
  hue is a hint, and these three stay distinguishable in a screenshot printed in black and
  white. The menu is deliberately five items (start, stop, open window, quit). **Quitting the
  tray leaves the engine running**: the only thing that stops the engine is the menu item that
  says so, because a container another process is using should not die when an icon is closed.
- **The window**: one window, and it is the list of containers — name, image, state, the
  daemon's own status sentence, and the ports. A published TCP port is a link that opens
  `http://localhost:<port>`; a port that is only exposed, or a UDP port, is plain text rather
  than a link that lands on nothing. Ports published on both address families are folded into
  one cell. WPF on the built-in .NET Fluent theme with `ThemeMode="System"`, so light and dark
  follow the OS with no extra package. Empty is a designed state: "the engine is not running"
  offers a Start button, "no containers" does not.
- **Nothing resident**: no Windows service and no scheduled task. Autostart is a single
  per-user registry value under the `Run` key, off unless the user turns it on, and turning it
  off removes the value rather than setting it to zero. The engine runs for exactly as long as
  a Windows process is holding it.
- **Tested against a clean Windows**: the product preflight is executed inside a Windows 11
  virtual machine through `vmrun` and what it said is read back, because a red row nobody has
  ever run is not a check.

## Non-goals (stated, not accidental)

- Feature parity with Docker Desktop.
- A fork of the engine — upstream Moby, unpatched, pinned by digest.
- macOS and Linux — the whole mechanism is WSL2 and a Windows named pipe.
- Telemetry, accounts or a sign-in.
- A resident background service.

## Installation

- **An installer, from the release page**:
  <https://github.com/alegauss/freewilly/releases/latest>. The asset carries its version in
  its name (`FreeWilly-Setup-<x.y.z>.exe`), and `SHA256SUMS.txt` beside it is what a
  download is checked against. Windows 10 build 19041 or later, 64-bit; no prerequisite,
  because the executable carries its own .NET runtime.
- **Per-user, no administrator prompt.** It installs into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FreeWilly`, which
  is what reaches a managed laptop. The WSL2 feature the engine needs may still want
  elevation of its own, and the installer runs the preflight and says so rather than failing
  halfway through a download.
- **Uninstalling asks about what was created.** The `freewilly` WSL2 distribution holds every
  image, container and volume, so it is never removed without a question, and an unattended
  uninstall keeps it.
- **From source** — `dotnet build`, then `build\build.cmd` for the single-file `.exe`; needs
  the .NET 10 SDK and Windows, and the installer additionally needs Inno Setup 6. Stated in
  the repository's own
  [README](https://github.com/alegauss/freewilly/blob/main/README.md#building). It is how a
  contributor works on this, and no longer how anybody has to run it.

## Layout

- `src/FreeWilly.Core` — the preflight judgement, the engine lifecycle and provisioning, and
  the Engine API client. No UI.
- `src/FreeWilly.Preflight` — `freewilly --preflight`, the standalone check.
- `src/FreeWilly.Engine` — `freewilly`, provisioning and the process that holds the
  engine and the pipe.
- `src/FreeWilly.Tray` — the WinForms tray icon and the WPF window.
- `site/` — the public site (Vite + React + Tailwind); its build emits this file, a Markdown
  twin per route and `manifest.json`.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` — governed by
  [roadkeep](https://github.com/alegauss/roadkeep) and written by that tool, not by hand.

## Data and network

- The only network traffic is downloading the three pinned artefacts from
  `dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org` and `download.docker.com`, during a provision the user asked for.
- Everything installed lives under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FreeWilly` (verified downloads, the
  distribution's disk, `bin\docker.exe`).
- Nothing is uploaded, nothing is measured, and there is no account.
